title: storage module: encrypted defaults, safe upgrades, and automated health checks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: deliver a hardened Terraform module for provisioning EBS, EFS, and S3 storage in VPC/private deployments that enforces encryption-by-default, provides safe in-place upgrade paths between module versions, and exposes automated health checks for runtime verification. This ticket covers module API, migration/upgrade utilities, CI validation, and runbook snippets for operators.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module defaults to CMKs or provider-managed encryption for EBS/EFS/S3 and exposes knobs for customer-supplied KMS keys.
2) Upgrade path documented and automated: terraform state migration plan, canary apply pattern, and rollback instructions.
3) CI contains plan-only and dry-run tests that detect destructive changes to snapshots and encryption.
4) Healthcheck Lambda/monitoring jobs (CloudWatch/Prometheus) template included and deployable via the module with sensible thresholds.
5) Integration test suite runs against a disposable VPC and validates snapshot lifecycle, encryption rotation, and cross-account replication settings.
6) Security review completed and docs linked in Confluence.
7) Ops runbook added to the module README and Console runbook folder.
tasks: Design module input API: kms_key_alias, encryption_mode (auto|cmk|none - default auto), snapshot_retention_days, cross_account_snapshot_role
Implement EBS construct with encrypted root/attach volumes, snapshot lifecycle resource, and automated snapshot tagging
Implement EFS construct: encrypted transit and at-rest, default backup policy using lifecycle manager
Implement S3 construct with bucket encryption block public access, default bucket policy, and optional replication configuration
Add state migration helper scripts (tfstate-migrate.sh) and example commands in upgrades.md
Create CI jobs: terraform fmt/validate/plan (against module examples) + PlanGuard - fail on encryption removal or snapshot-deletion diffs
Add healthcheck resources: Lambda that verifies latest snapshot timestamps, KMS key rotation status, and EFS mountiness; optional Prometheus exporter
Write integration tests and a disposable VPC harness in GitHub Actions + terraform-apply/teardown
Draft operator runbook: canary apply steps, preflight checks, failure modes and rollback commands
Coordinate security review and add KMS key policy templates for cross-account use

notes: Design decisions: prefer provider-managed CMKs for hosted customers; default to customer-managed CMK for Private deployments when kms_key_alias is provided. Avoid in-place KMS alias swaps without snapshot re-encryption; we instead create new keys and rotate references with a safe handover. Module exposes 'upgrade_plan_check' output which enumerates any destructive actions the plan would perform to assist canary applications.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental removal of encryption or snapshot deletion during module upgrades. Mitigation: PlanGuard in CI blocks merges with destructive changes, canary apply workflow in infra repo, and manual approval required for any plan that touches encryption resources. Backfill policy for older snapshots includes a migration job, not an automated destructive re-write.
operator_runbook_summary: Canary flow: 1) run ./tfstate-migrate.sh --dry-run against staging state, 2) apply module in staging VPC, 3) run healthcheck job and validate metrics, 4) target 1% of controls plane hosts for canary in production with approval, 5) if failures, run tf rollback plan from saved workspace snapshot.
integration_test_summary: Tests provision a disposable VPC, create volumes & buckets, snapshot them, rotate a test CMK, and assert that snapshots remain accessible and newest snapshots have expected tags and encryption metadata. Tests run nightly and on PRs affecting the module.
implementation_notes: Prefer Terraform 1.6+ to use provider-sensitive variables and stronger state migration helpers. Use sentinel/OPA policies in CI to codify 'no encryption removal' rule. Provide a backward-compatible v1->v2 upgrade guide in UPGRADES.md. Keep examples folder with 'private' and 'hosted' usage patterns.
